Capital expenditures were $45.2 billion, as some third-party capacity deliveries we expected in Q1 were delayed. Roughly three quarters of our capex was for short-lived assets, primarily CPUs and GPUs, including higher memory and storage costs, as we continue to invest in the infrastructure required for our customers to build and scale AI applications.

Now, moving to the outlook for our second quarter, which unless specifically noted otherwise, is on a US dollar basis.

Based on current rates, we expect FX to have no meaningful impact on total revenue, COGS or operating expense growth, or on revenue growth in either segment.

Starting with segment guidance.

We expect revenue from Agents and Infra of $80.1 to $80.7 billion, or growth of 24 to 25%.

In commercial bookings, we expect healthy growth in our commercial sales motions, though results will be impacted by the significant Azure commitments signed in the prior year. Timing related to significant Azure commitments like these will result in material volatility in bookings, making quarterly growth rates less indicative of underlying sales execution.

In Azure, we expect revenue growth of 49 to 50% in constant currency with continued efficiency gains across our CPU and GPU fleet helping to offset some 3P GPU as a service contracts that have been delayed to H2. Customer demand continues to exceed available supply. And looking beyond Q2, year-over-year growth will continue to reflect the timing and scale of engineering efficiencies delivered in the quarter, and new capacity adds, as well as a strong prior-year comparable that included accelerating growth in the second half.

In M365 Commercial cloud, we expect growth of approximately 19% in constant currency, with FX expected to reduce reported growth by less than a point. We expect continued momentum across our premium per-seat offerings and usage-based offerings, along with some improvement in execution across E3 and our standalone SKUs. Growth will be driven primarily by ARPU, with additional contribution from seats. And we continue to expect revenue growth to accelerate through the year.

Productivity and server licensing revenue should decline in the mid to high-single digits, down sequentially due to a lower expected mix of contracts that carry higher in-period revenue recognition. Quarterly growth can vary materially based on contract mix, product launch timing, and other transactional purchasing trends.

In Industry solutions cloud, we expect revenue growth to be in the mid to high-single digits with continued impact from the bookings trends noted earlier.

And in Frontier and support services, we expect revenue to grow in the low to mid-single digits.

In devices and consumer, we expect revenue to be $15.9 to $16.4 billion.

Search advertising revenue ex-TAC growth should be in the low-double digits driven by consistent trends in rate and volume, with overall search and advertising revenue expected to grow at a similar rate.

And in XBOX content and services, we expect revenue growth to be in the mid to high-single digits, up sequentially driven by the timing of content launches across both third- and first-party. With content launch patterns through the year, we expect growth to be strongest in the second quarter, with some deceleration in Q3 and further moderation in Q4. Hardware revenue in Q2 should decline year-over-year.

Windows OEM and Devices revenue should decline in the mid-thirties. Growth will continue to be impacted by elevated inventory levels, PC market demand, and a prior-year comparable that benefited from Windows 10 end of support. As in prior quarters, the range of potential outcomes remains wider than normal. We expect these trends to continue through the rest of this fiscal year.

We expect COGS of $32.7 to $32.9 billion, or growth of 26 to 27%. And operating expense of $18.5 to $18.6 billion or growth of 9% driven by continued investment in R&D compute capacity and talent. Our cost guidance across both COGS and OpEx includes an estimate for the recently announced employee voluntary exit offer. Operating margins should be down slightly year-over-year.

Excluding any impact from our investments in OpenAI, other income and expense is expected to be roughly negative $300 million as interest income will be more than offset by interest expense, which includes the interest payments related to datacenter finance leases.

And we expect our Q2 effective tax rate to be approximately 20%.

In Q2, we expect CapEx spend will be over $50 billion. Therefore, for the calendar year, spend should be approximately $170 billion due to the 3P capacity delays noted earlier. In the second half of the fiscal year, we currently expect CapEx spend to accelerate primarily from CPUs, inclusive of higher memory and storage costs, and GPUs, as well as the 3P capacity deliveries that shifted to H2. And as we continue to improve the efficiency of our infrastructure, each dollar of capex has the potential to support more revenue and higher returns over time.

Given our strong business performance, we expect to continue to remain free cash flow positive in FY27. To complement cash generated by the business and preserve financial flexibility, we will access additional sources of funding when we believe it is attractive to do so.
